claim: The US Food and Drug Administration authorized COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) therapy for hospitalized COVID-19 patients via the Expanded Access Program (EAP) and the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA).
source: The US Food and Drug Administration authorized COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) therapy for hospitalized COVID-19 patients via the Expanded Access Program (EAP) and the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), leading to use in about 500,000 patients during the first year of the pandemic for the USA.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and introduction, with references to regulatory documents.

claim: About 500,000 patients received CCP during the first year of the pandemic in the USA.
source: The US Food and Drug Administration authorized COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) therapy for hospitalized COVID-19 patients via the Expanded Access Program (EAP) and the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), leading to use in about 500,000 patients during the first year of the pandemic for the USA.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the scale of CCP usage based on the study's data collection.

claim: CCP usage per admission peaked in Fall 2020, with more than 40% of inpatients estimated to have received CCP between late September and early November 2020.
source: CCP usage per admission peaked in Fall 2020, with more than 40% of inpatients estimated to have received CCP between late September and early November 2020.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by data presented in Figure 2.

claim: After randomized controlled trials failed to show a reduction in mortality, CCP usage per admission declined steadily to a nadir of less than 10% in March 2021.
source: However, after randomized controlled trials failed to show a reduction in mortality, CCP usage per admission declined steadily to a nadir of less than 10% in March 2021.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by temporal data in the manuscript.

claim: There was a strong inverse correlation (r = −0.52, p=0.002) between CCP usage per hospital admission and deaths occurring 2 weeks after admission.
source: We found a strong inverse correlation (r = −0.52, p=0.002) between CCP usage per hospital admission and deaths occurring 2 weeks after admission, and this finding was robust to examination of deaths taking place 1, 2, or 3 weeks after admission.
evidence: This correlation is explicitly stated in the abstract and shown in Figure 3 with statistical analysis.

claim: The inverse correlation between CCP use and mortality was robust to examination of deaths taking place 1, 2, or 3 weeks after admission.
source: We found a strong inverse correlation (r = −0.52, p=0.002) between CCP usage per hospital admission and deaths occurring 2 weeks after admission, and this finding was robust to examination of deaths taking place 1, 2, or 3 weeks after admission.
evidence: This robustness is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Changes in the number of hospital admissions, SARS-CoV-2 variants, and age of patients could not explain the inverse correlation findings.
source: Changes in the number of hospital admissions, SARS-CoV-2 variants, and age of patients could not explain these findings.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and elaborated in the discussion with supporting analyses.

claim: The retreat from CCP usage might have resulted in as many as 29,000 excess deaths from mid-November 2020 to February 2021.
source: The retreat from CCP usage might have resulted in as many as 29,000 excess deaths from mid-November 2020 to February 2021.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and calculated using the linear model described in the methods and results.

claim: The first transfusion under the Expanded Access Program occurred in early April 2020.
source: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory oversight was provided first by its Expanded Access Program (EAP) in partnership with the Mayo Clinic, with first transfusion on early April 2020 (Senefeld et al., 2021), and then by its Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) of August 23, 2020, both of which restricted CCP use to hospitalized patients (Anonymous, 2021b).
evidence: This is directly stated with a citation to Senefeld et al., 2021.

claim: The Emergency Use Authorization for CCP was issued on August 23, 2020.
source: US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory oversight was provided first by its Expanded Access Program (EAP) in partnership with the Mayo Clinic, with first transfusion on early April 2020 (Senefeld et al., 2021), and then by its Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) of August 23, 2020, both of which restricted CCP use to hospitalized patients (Anonymous, 2021b).
evidence: This is explicitly stated with a citation to Anonymous, 2021b.

claim: Both the EAP and EUA restricted CCP use to hospitalized patients.

evidence: This is directly stated in the introduction.

claim: CCP was demonstrated to be safe by the Summer of 2020.
source: The demonstration by the Summer of 2020 that CCP was safe (Joyner et al., 2020a; Joyner et al., 2020b), that antibody concentration in plasma correlated with survival in people treated before mechanical ventilation (Joyner et al., 2021) along with initial suggestions of efficacy (Li et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2020; Salazar et al., 2020), boosted its use.
evidence: This is stated with citations to Joyner et al., 2020a and 2020b.

claim: Antibody concentration in plasma correlated with survival in people treated before mechanical ventilation.
source: The demonstration by the Summer of 2020 that CCP was safe (Joyner et al., 2020a; Joyner et al., 2020b), that antibody concentration in plasma correlated with survival in people treated before mechanical ventilation (Joyner et al., 2021) along with initial suggestions of efficacy (Li et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2020; Salazar et al., 2020), boosted its use.
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Joyner et al., 2021.

claim: Early RCTs of CCP were generally trending positively but were inconclusive, mostly due to small size or premature termination as the epidemic abated in the early surge regions.
source: Nonetheless, the use of CCP rose rapidly without the ideal evidence base of efficacy from randomized controlled clinical trials (RCTs), since early RCTs though generally trending positively were inconclusive, mostly due to small size or premature termination as the epidemic abated in the early surge regions (Casadevall et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Casadevall et al., 2020.

claim: Several larger RCTs reported no mortality benefit from CCP.

claim: The negative RCTs were undertaken in hospitalized patients treated late in the course of disease and some used plasma with variable antibody levels.
source: However, these latter trials were undertaken in hospitalized patients treated late in the course of disease and some used plasma with variable antibody levels (Casadevall et al., 2020), and contrasted with a highly successful trial in elderly patients treated within 3 days of illness onset prior to hospitalization (Libster et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with citations to Casadevall et al., 2020 and Libster et al., 2021.

claim: A trial in elderly patients treated within 3 days of illness onset prior to hospitalization was highly successful.
source: However, these latter trials were undertaken in hospitalized patients treated late in the course of disease and some used plasma with variable antibody levels (Casadevall et al., 2020), and contrasted with a highly successful trial in elderly patients treated within 3 days of illness onset prior to hospitalization (Libster et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Libster et al., 2021.

claim: The British Medical Journal called CCP 'ineffective'.
source: Despite potential explanations for the negative studies, the results of these studies were sometimes accompanied by editorials that reinforced the message of futility with the British Medical Journal calling CCP 'ineffective' (Pathak, 2020), Nature Biotechnology reported that CCP fell 'flat' (Sheridan, 2020), and JAMA published a meta-analysis of RCT concluding that there was no evidence of benefit from CCP therapy (Janiaud et al., 2021).

claim: Nature Biotechnology reported that CCP fell 'flat'.

source: On March 13, 2021, the New York Times reported that COVID-19 mortality remained high with nearly 1500 daily deaths despite a drop in the number of new infections since earlier in the year (Leatherby, 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Leatherby, 2021.

claim: Treatment outcomes for COVID-19 worsened for the last 2 months of 2020.
source: Consistent with this report, an analysis of treatment outcomes found that they worsened for the last 2 months of 2020 (Garg et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated with a citation to Garg et al., 2021.

claim: There was a powerful and significant correlation (Spearman's rho = 0.953, p<0.001) between the weekly counts of units distributed in the USA and those used to treat patients as part of the EAP between April 6 and August 23, 2020.
source: There was a powerful and significant correlation between the weekly counts of units distributed in the USA and those used to treat patients as part of the EAP between April 6 and August 23, 2020 (Spearman's rho = 0.953, p<0.001) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: The vast majority (>95%) of all convalescent plasma administered was likely captured in this analysis.
source: In this context, the vast majority (>95%) of all convalescent plasma (CP) administered was likely captured in this analysis (Senefeld et al., 2021).

claim: The overwhelming majority of COVID-19 deaths occur in hospitals.
source: Since the overwhelming majority of COVID-19 deaths occur in hospitals (Chua et al., 2021; Chuzi et al., 2020), since CCP is only authorized for use in hospitals, and since death generally occurs a few days to weeks after admission, mortality was adjusted for the time lag between admission and death.
evidence: This is stated with citations to Chua et al., 2021 and Chuzi et al., 2020.

claim: Distribution of CCP to hospitals rose to 25,000–30,000 weekly units by the December 2020 to January 2021 time period.
source: Distribution of CCP to hospitals rose to 25,000–30,000 weekly units by the December 2020 to January 2021 time period, but this rise in plasma distribution largely reflected the great increase in hospital admissions for COVID in those months (Figure 1).

claim: Peak CCP utilization per capita occurred in early October 2020.
source: When CCP distributions are analyzed as a function of the number of new hospital admissions per week, peak utilization per capita occurred much earlier, in early October 2020 and declined sharply in the following months (Figure 2).

claim: There is no significant correlation between shifted mortality and the percent of hospitalized patients 65+ each week, suggesting changes in mortality are not explainable by an increase in hospitalized high-risk patients.
source: There is no significant correlation between the two variables, suggesting changes in mortality are not explainable by an increase in hospitalized high-risk patients.

source: The linear model using the CCP utilization ratio to predict the CFR fits the data well in that this model explained 25% (R2 = 0.254) of the variance of CFR using only the CCP utilization ratio.
